INDEPENDENT · UNOFFICIAL FIELD GUIDE

Azeroth Survivors Rogue build

Last updated: October 29, 2026

Field guide

What is Azeroth Survivors?How to playBuildsTier listDownload & fixesSafety checkTalent treeLuck

Rogue melts bosses and punishes surround mistakes. The burst is real, but the class demands deliberate circling: if you let the wave close from two sides, the health pool does not buy you enough time. It is the pick for players who already read enemy movement, not for a first clear.

Build phases

0–3 min

Take an area card before single-target burst so the first wave stays manageable.

3–8 min

Commit to one carry and one survival or movement tool. Circle deliberately so enemies cannot close from two sides.

8–15 min

Rank up the carry, then cooldown reduction; concentrate burst into boss openings.

Boss notes

Circle with an exit in view. The burst payoff is strongest when you can keep attacking without being surrounded.

Common mistakes

Letting waves close from two sides. Prioritizing single-target cards before area coverage. Using mobility to chase damage.

Skill priority

  • Early area coverage.
  • One burst carry.
  • One survival or movement tool.
  • Carry ranks and cooldown reduction.

Passive priority

  1. Blessing of Might — +10% all damage per rank, +50% at rank 5. It helps every build; take it first.
  2. Arcane Intellect — 8% faster recharge per rank, 40% at rank 5, total capped at 65%.
  3. Amplify Magic — +10% area size per rank, +50% at rank 5. Huge for Flamestrike, Consecration, Volley.
  4. Blessing of Wisdom — +8% experience per rank, +40% at rank 5. Take it early or not at all.
  5. Power Word: Fortitude — +20% max health per rank, +100% at rank 5. Buffer on squishier classes.
  • See the full passive priority and stat caps

FAQ

Is Rogue a good first-clear choice?

Read the Rogue trade-off above and the tier list. Warrior or Paladin remains the forgiving first-clear starting point.

What should I take in the first three minutes?

Take an area card before single-target burst so the first wave stays manageable.

When should I spend rerolls?

Use the level 6–12 commitment window, rather than spending rerolls in the first three levels.

What is the main Rogue mistake?

Letting waves close from two sides. Prioritizing single-target cards before area coverage. Using mobility to chase damage.
